svg.title: Artificial Intelligence Models: source-backed reference mind map
svg.desc: A top-down mind map. The grouping is an editorial synthesis, not an official or exhaustive standard. Concepts overlap. Each source marker opens a primary publication, author textbook or official documentation.

text.tspan: A I / R E F E R E N C E M A P
A model can occupy several branches at once; axes are not mutually exclusive.

g.title: Logical Representations: Propositional and first-order representations. Source: AI: A Modern Approach, 4th ed.
Rule-Based Models: Explicit rules for inference. Source: AI: A Modern Approach, 4th ed.
Linear & Logistic Models: Linear predictors and linked probabilities. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Kernel Methods: Support vector machines; Gaussian processes. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Decision Trees & Ensembles: Trees; random forests; gradient boosting. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Nearest-Neighbor Models: Predictions from nearby observations. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Bayesian Networks: Directed probabilistic dependencies. Source: AI: A Modern Approach, 4th ed.
Hidden Markov Models: Latent state transitions and emissions. Source: AI: A Modern Approach, 4th ed.
Gaussian Mixture Models: Mixtures of component distributions. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Linear Factor Models: PCA and related latent-factor models. Source: Deep Learning
Neural Networks: Architectures expanded in the next branch. Source: Deep Learning

text.tspan: Architectures expanded in the next branch

g.title: Multilayer Perceptrons: Feedforward, densely connected layers. Source: Deep Learning
Convolutional Networks: Shared filters over structured inputs. Source: Deep Learning
Recurrent Networks: Recurrent state; LSTM and GRU variants. Source: Speech and Language Processing

text.tspan: Recurrent state; LSTM and GRU variants

g.title: Transformers: Attention-based representation processing. Source: Attention Is All You Need
Graph Neural Networks: Computation over nodes and edges. Source: Graph Convolutional Networks
State-Space Networks: Structured sequence state dynamics. Source: Mamba
Encoder-Only: Contextual representations of inputs. Source: Transformer Architectures
Decoder-Only: Causal sequence generation. Source: Transformer Architectures
Encoder–Decoder: Input encoding with output generation. Source: Transformer Architectures
Mixture of Experts: Routing to specialized subnetworks. Source: Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts

text.tspan: Where does the learning signal come from?

g.title: Supervised Learning: Labeled input–target examples. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Unsupervised Learning: Structure without externally supplied targets. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Semi-Supervised Learning: Labeled and unlabeled examples together. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Self-Supervised Learning: Targets derived from the observations. Source: SimCLR
Reinforcement Learning: Actions evaluated through reward signals. Source: AI: A Modern Approach, 4th ed.

a.aria-label: Paradigms Can Be Combined: open source 35

g.title: Paradigms Can Be Combined: A single model can use several stages. Source: InstructGPT

text.tspan: A single model can use several stages

g.title: Learning Signals Can Overlap: These labels are not mutually exclusive

text.tspan: These labels are not mutually exclusive
How is a data distribution represented?

g.title: Autoregressive Models: Factorization into conditional predictions. Source: Deep Learning
Variational Autoencoders: Latent variables with variational inference. Source: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
Generative Adversarial Networks: Generator trained against a discriminator. Source: Generative Adversarial Networks
Diffusion Models: Generation through learned denoising. Source: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
Normalizing Flows: Invertible distribution transformations. Source: Variational Inference with Normalizing Flows
Energy-Based Models: Compatibility encoded by an energy function. Source: Deep Learning

text.tspan: Compatibility encoded by an energy function

g.title: Flow Matching: Vector-field training for continuous flows. Source: Flow Matching
Formulation and Architecture: Separate, potentially overlapping axes

text.tspan: What can the model receive or produce?

g.title: Text: Natural-language sequences. Source: Hugging Face Tasks
Code: Programming-language sequences. Source: CodeXGLUE
Images: Still visual observations. Source: Hugging Face Tasks
Video: Sequences of visual frames. Source: Hugging Face Tasks
Speech & Audio: Spoken language and other sounds. Source: SUPERB
Tabular Data: Records with defined feature columns. Source: scikit-learn User Guide
Time Series: Time-indexed measurements. Source: sktime API Reference
Graphs: Entities connected through relations. Source: Open Graph Benchmark
3D Representations: Shapes, meshes and spatial fields. Source: Shap-E
Multimodal Models: Several modalities within one model. Source: Foundation Models

text.tspan: How is the model prepared and specialized?

g.title: Foundation-Model Pretraining: Broad training for downstream adaptation. Source: Foundation Models
Task-Specific Fine-Tuning: Update parameters for a target task. Source: Transformer Architectures

text.tspan: Update parameters for a target task

g.title: Instruction Tuning: Supervised learning from instructions. Source: InstructGPT
Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA): Train small low-rank parameter updates. Source: LoRA

a.aria-label: RL from Human Feedback: open source 35

g.title: RL from Human Feedback: Reward-based tuning from human preferences. Source: InstructGPT
Direct Preference Optimization: Optimize directly from preference pairs. Source: Direct Preference Optimization
Knowledge Distillation: Transfer behavior from teacher to student. Source: Knowledge Distillation

text.tspan: Transfer behavior from teacher to student

Model / Algorithm Tasks: Evaluate a defined input–output mapping. Source: Hugging Face Tasks
System-Level Tasks: Evaluate end-to-end task completion. Source: OSWorld

a.aria-label: Structured Decision Models: open source S49

g.title: Structured Decision Models: Declared answer spaces → typed decisions and probabilities. Source: S49
Direct Inference (System 1-style): Focused prediction without a separate deliberation or search stage. Source: S50
Deliberative Inference (System 2-style): Intermediate reasoning, search or verification during inference. Source: S51

a.aria-label: Hybrid / Adaptive Inference: open source S52

g.title: Hybrid / Adaptive Inference: Documented mode switching or adaptive inference procedures. Source: S52

text.tspan: Modes may overlap. A short answer or a
fast response does not establish a mode.
HOW TO READ • A model family, architecture, learning signal, data modality and task describe different properties.
For example: a model may be a Transformer, self-supervised during pretraining, multimodal, and adapted for question answering.
8 classification axes / 54 selected concepts / companion map: 87 task entries
S01–S53 are clickable source references. Sources: author textbooks, original papers and official documentation. Updated 25 October 2026.
